title: asyncio-starvation-request-parse-scratchpad
content:
Quick summary:
This is an exploratory scratchpad for a recurring small-request latency spike we see in prod where the Python request parsing and tokenization stage sometimes stalls the event loop for 5–30ms. The user-visible symptom: p50 is fine but p99/p999 for small payloads (<1KB) spikes. Hypothesis: asyncio event loop starvation due to synchronous CPU-bound parse/tokenize work + threadpool handoff backpressure + occasional syscalls that block the loop (epoll wake ordering).

Observations so far (raw):
- Repro on dev with synthetic traffic (1000 rps, 1–2 token requests, seq_len 32) using local runner. p99 ~ 18ms (target 8ms).
- py-spy (sampling) shows frequent stacks in parse_request -> json.loads -> _iter_* and in tokenizer.c extension when present.
- When the tokenization path uses Rust FFI (fastjson/c-ext), the time slices move but we still observe 5–8ms tail events where the asyncio loop appears not to schedule other tasks.
- psutil & top: CPU saturates single core during spikes. Threads in process show one busy worker thread and one event-loop thread stuck.

Detailed traces & commands performed:
- Synthetic load: ./tools/loadgen --qps 1000 --payload small.json --concurrency 8 --duration 120s
- py-spy record -o spike.svg --pid $PID --native --sleep 0.005 --subprocesses (samples show heavy python frames in request_parse.py:parse_headers and tokenizer.py:tokenize_batch)
- sudo perf record -F 4000 -p $PID -g -- sleep 30; perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded; flamegraph.pl out.folded > perf-spike.svg
- bcc run (off-cpu) shows threads sleeping on futex, but not consistently correlated with spikes.
- Traces instrumented with tracepoints (loop.time() markers) show loop callbacks delayed by caller contexts that block for >10ms.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Parse/tokenize synchronous CPU bursts block loop when executed inline in the loop thread (we call json.loads or tokenizer in request handler before offloading).
2) ThreadPoolExecutor handoff latency: using default threadpool sometimes queues tasks; when pool is saturated wake ordering causes callback invoked in loop later (context switch/wakeup jitter).
3) Syscall ordering / epoll race: long syscall from C-extension (tokenizer) blocks wake-up of loop fd due to kernel scheduler ordering on single core.
4) GIL-related pauses: Python C extension reacquires GIL in C path causing stalls visible to the main thread.

Experiments run and results:
- Move parse to run_in_executor (ThreadPoolExecutor) for test handlers: improved p99 slightly from 18ms -> 12ms, but occasional 25ms spikes remain. Suggests not entirely fixed.
- Increase ThreadPoolExecutor max_workers from 16 -> 64 in dev: p99 improved but CPU profile shows more cores used and total CPU cost up. Not ideal for cost model.
- Replace json.loads with orjson: ~30% reduction in parse time on average; p99 reduced further to ~9ms but tail still exists.
- Replace Python tokenizer with Rust FFI prototype with release build and GIL release: average tokenization down by 3x, but saw rare 15–30ms stalls apparently correlated with heap allocation pauses in extension (needs deeper eBPF).
- Force affinity: pin event loop thread to a dedicated core and offload work to other cores -> tail reduced but still present when single-core load high (confirms kernel scheduling influence).

Notes from sampling artifacts (high level):
- Flamegraphs show two classes of spikes: (A) long user CPU stacks in parse/tokenize (expected), (B) short awake->sleep loops where the loop didn't poll for epoll events for 6–20ms (harder to explain).
- The 'awake->sleep' micro-pattern often starts with a small function call that triggers a blocking C-call (e.g. c_ext_tokenize) that holds the CPU and sometimes the GIL for the duration.

Open microtests to run next (actionable):
- Add eBPF sched/sched_wake trace to correlate wakeup latency to the thread that performed syscall. Quick probe: run trace that records timestamp of wake/wake_up_new and correlate to our process threads. (ticket: INF-2398)
- Instrument loop with high-res timestamps at scheduling boundaries to record exact time spent between poll returns and callback entry. (simple traces in asyncio: loop._run_once patched)
- Create a tiny reproducer that alternates between a noop sleep and a heavy parse to reproduce wake ordering on 1 core. If reproducible, can open a kernel issue or apply local mitigation (yield before offload).
- Try moving synchronous parse into ProcessPoolExecutor for a short test to see if GIL-bound C-extensions are causing main-thread stalls. Downsides: IPC cost for small payloads but may avoid GIL scheduling.
- Experiment with having parse/tokenize do periodic async-yield (await asyncio.sleep(0)) if done inline — tradeoff throughput for less tail.

Immediate mitigations for product rollout (low-risk):
- Use orjson where possible for request parsing (config flag per route).
- Default to run_in_executor for user-provided parsers unless handler opts-in for inline processing.
- Add telemetry: count occurrences of loop-delay >5ms per request, annotate traces with parse-mode (inline/offload/ffi).

Unresolved questions / weirdness:
- We still see spikes when the tokenization path is fully offloaded to threads, suggesting that handoff latency + wake ordering still imposes tail cost. Why does moving to executor sometimes increase tail? Possibly because when we offload, the main loop does a sleep/poll and relies on thread wake to re-notify; if wake happens slightly later due to kernel scheduler the loop stays sleeping until next wake.
- C-extension that supposedly releases GIL may still interact badly with kernel preemption when performing many small syscalls (alloc/free). Need to instrument malloc/free in extension paths.

Quick checklist (who/what):
- [ ] Liam: add eBPF trace for sched_wake correlation (INF-2398)
- [ ] Noah: build minimal single-core reproducer and run with perf + flamegraph
- [ ] Asha: add loop instrumentation and light telemetry to prod dev cluster (feature flag) to collect loop-delay histograms for 2 days
- [ ] Eng: consider defaulting parsing to orjson and offloading for routes with <500B payloads (A/B test)

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally messy. Save final run notes into a postmortem once we have deterministic reproducer. Link to apm traces: JIRA-INF-2387 has sample spans; correlate with infra metrics (cpu steal, irq).

References & links:
- internal: github PR 912 (experiment branch with process pool prototype)
- internal: esp signal in slack thread (see linked_artifacts)

End of scratchpad.

-- Asha
